title: mesh-bus data ontology
description: Data atoms organized by OSI encapsulation vocabulary. For each layer: PCI = the control data this layer authors and owns (its own header); SDU = the entire PDU handed down from the layer above, carried opaque, never inspected; PDU = SDU + PCI, the unit this layer hands down (which becomes the next layer's SDU). The boundary rule is exactly the SDU contract: a layer reads and authors only its own PCI; the SDU stays opaque. This is why L7 is the complete data: L7 has no upper layer, so its PDU is the un-encapsulated whole; each descent re-frames the upper PDU as this layer's opaque SDU and adds only this layer's PCI. Self-contained: no $ref to any existing contract.
encapsulation_chain: L7.pdu -> L6.sdu ; L6.pdu -> L5.sdu ; L5.pdu -> L4.sdu ; L4.pdu -> substrate.sdu ; substrate.pdu -> wire. Bottom-up reverses it: each layer strips its PCI and surfaces its SDU upward until L7 reassembles the complete data.

L7_application_participant.pdu_name: Event{ payload, meta } driving run_pipeline + the L5 session it opens
L7_application_participant.sdu: raw external-protocol application bytes the adapter carries (no upper bus layer; this is the data origin)

pci.intent_target: destination the application asked to reach (host:port, domain, mesh route)
pci.credential: auth material presented or required by the adapter (SOCKS5 user/pass, mesh peer key id)
pci.route_group: named candidate-exit grouping requested by the participant
pci.policy_ref_origin: the opaque policy token as authored by the participant before it descends
pci.host_sni_url: L7-only naming surface (HTTP host header, TLS SNI, request URL) — never read below L7

L7_application_participant.boundary: authors only the bus-semantic PCI above; the application payload is its SDU and is carried opaque downward

L6_transform.pdu_name: transformed/sealed frame = PCI header + transformed inner
L6_transform.sdu: L7 PDU (opaque payload bytes; core copies/forwards/seals but never parses)

pci.fragment_metadata: { group_id, fragment_id, seq, total, offset, deadline_ms, checksum }
pci.meshsec_epoch_key_state: HKDF-SHA256 epoch-derived key material per configured peer (KeyEpoch, peer key state)
pci.meshsec_nonce_counter: per-egress / per-matched-peer Arc<AtomicU64> counter feeding the XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce
pci.meshsec_replay_window: 1024-bit post-AEAD-auth replay window per peer epoch boot_salt
pci.meshsec_envelope_header: meshsec_envelope_v1: 22-byte header + padding-bucket framing wrapping the sealed inner

L6_transform.boundary: owns transform metadata + envelope header (PCI); core validates metadata shape only and runs no transform algorithm; the SDU and the sealed inner stay opaque to every layer below

pci.bus_session_info: { session_id, flow_id, schedule_mode, paths[], primary, path_trace[], started_at_ms }
pci.schedule_mode: Ordered | Replicate | Stripe (the realized mode for this session)

L5_session.boundary: authors session identity + path lifecycle (PCI); carries the L6 PDU as opaque SDU

L4_forwarding.pdu_name: dispatched flow on the selected exit

pci.flow_id: identity born at first successful Open
pci.rank_context: { packet_id, flow_id, session_id, target, traffic_class, policy_ref, deadline_ms, schedule_hint, flow_semantics, return_semantics, source_key, target_key }
pci.schedule_hint: Auto | SinglePath | { FanOut, k } | { Stripe, n }
pci.capabilities: exit capability set used for candidate matching
pci.path_trace: running list of L4-selected exits for the flow (authored here by dispatch; L5 only re-exposes it inside bus_session_info)
pci.close_reason: flow termination cause (TtlExpired, NoUsableExit, UpstreamEof, ReaderClosed, ConnectionReset, ...)
pci.flow_pin: L4-stored exit affinity (cross-layer: stored in L4 PCI, value supplied by the L7 pipeline)

L4_forwarding.boundary: routes on flow-native PCI only; must not read any L7 naming atom (host/SNI/URL/intent); the L5 PDU is opaque SDU

substrate_tcp_udp.holder: OS socket layer surfaced by the egress driver
substrate_tcp_udp.pdu_name: TCP segment / UDP datagram on the wire

pci.byte_counters: raw bytes moved on the socket (pre-accounting)

substrate_tcp_udp.boundary: owns wire endpoints + raw byte movement (PCI); holds no flow/session/transform identity; the L4 PDU is opaque SDU

kernel_runtime_carrier.role: not a layer in the encapsulation chain — it is the carrier; Frame is the PDU container and Frame.payload is by definition the SDU slot, which is why it is opaque

pci.frame: carrier unit; the payload field is the SDU and is never inspected by the kernel
pci.dataplane_shape: Forwarder | DatagramForwarder | FrameRouter (derived once at first Open)
pci.bus_event: SessionOpened | SessionClosed | Core{ type_id ∈ [FlowOpened,FlowPathChanged,FlowClosed,PathIoError], payload, at_ns }
pci.typed_map: kernel-side hot metadata struct (net/transport/policy/auth/trace + ext) — keys are kernel-owned PCI, values are the owning layer's PCI

kernel_runtime_carrier.boundary: moves PDUs between layers without owning layer-native meaning; the payload SDU stays opaque

cross_layer_pci.note: OSI keeps PCI strictly per-layer; TCP/IP collapses layers so a few atoms are authored in one layer's PCI yet valued or carried elsewhere. Recorded as fact.
cross_layer_pci.flow_pin: lives in L4 PCI; value supplied by the L7 pipeline
cross_layer_pci.policy_ref: authored as L7 PCI; carried as an opaque token inside lower-layer SDU framing, never decoded below L7

metadata_namespace_ownership.note: Per-namespace authoring layer and write/read roles. `source_initial_writes_allowed` is the closed set an L7 application-source projection (pipeline.source.initial_writes / SourceSpec.initial_writes) may pre-write at ingress; lower-layer L4-control PCI is authored only by the sanctioned in-pipeline projection hook, never by operator config.

conformance_audit.scope: crates/mesh-bus-core/src — boundary audit of actual code against this ontology; read-only, no code changed
invariants_confirmed_clean: L6 transform is algorithm-free: transport/transform/ holds only types + validate_fragment (pure shape check); MeshSec algorithm lives in lib/mb-proto-mesh, outside core
kernel L7-opacity: kernel/ contains no socks/http/tls/quic identifier (guarded by tests/kernel_invariant.rs)
Frame.payload SDU-opacity: whole-crate access is .len() or whole-move only; observers read the typed ObservationEnvelope (allowed payload_bytes), not opaque bytes

findings.F1_ontology_self_correction_resolved: path_trace was mis-assigned to L5 PCI; dispatch.rs:252,441 shows L4 dispatch authors it (selected-exit history). Reassigned to L4 PCI; L5 only re-exposes it via bus_session_info. Fixed in this file.
findings.F2_layer_inversion_resolved: FlowId is now opaque (DefaultHasher over session_id+host+port, no cleartext L7 host) and minted through the single L4-owned FlowId::mint_for; transport/session/data_handle.rs L5 site now carries (does not author) the L4 identity. Full FlowId-returned-through-ReturnEvent::Connected channel plumbing remains a documented follow-up (posture deeper than this conformance pass).
findings.F3_carrier_key_smell_open: kernel/dispatch.rs:84,94,278,329,369 and forwarder.rs:60,97 — carrier keys runtime maps and tracing on L5 session_id. Permitted by the current 'session_id as generic correlation key' invariant, so not a hard violation; open decision: keep pragmatic vs introduce a carrier-native key. Code change deferred (release track frozen).
findings.F4_mesh_peer_budget_resolved: mesh-bus-egress-mesh-peer-udp advertised datagram budget is now MeshSec-aware (MESHSEC_MAX_CLEAR_LEN - frame overhead when sealed) instead of a fixed 65_000 (~64x over-advertise → silent drop); QUIC StreamOpen.source_node_id is the configured local node id, not a hardcoded "local".

conformance_audit.note: F2 and F4 are resolved at functional-verification level (FlowId opaque + L4-owned mint with L5 carry-not-author; mesh-peer advertised budget MeshSec-aware + QUIC source_node_id from cfg.node.id); F3 (carrier maps/tracing keyed on L5 session_id) stays a permitted open decision under the 'session_id as generic correlation key' invariant; the FlowId minted-and-returned through ReturnEvent::Connected channel is the remaining documented follow-up. M8-M12 release track stays frozen pending separate user decision.
